overview: This Senate resolution marks January 27, 2025, as the 80th anniversary of the liberation of the Auschwitz death camp in Nazi-occupied Poland by Allied forces at the end of World War II, and as International Holocaust Remembrance Day, a date set by the United Nations. It recalls that about 1.1 million people were murdered at Auschwitz, most of them Jewish, along with Poles, Romani people, Soviet prisoners, people with disabilities, and others. It calls on Americans to remember the six million Jews and all other victims of the Holocaust, honors survivors, urges continued work against genocide and persecution, and recommits the Senate to fighting antisemitism. It notes a recent rise in antisemitic incidents in the United States. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 27, 2025.
for: Supporters say formally remembering the Holocaust as the last survivors pass away helps keep its lessons alive and signals a firm stand against rising antisemitism.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, spending, or specific program for fighting antisemitism.
